title: MRAgent — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn. Each node states both sides; the lane says which stage of the pipeline the divergence sits in.
source: paper arXiv:2606.06036v1 (Ji et al.)  ×  MRAgent @ 7441506   ·   servers/mragent/verification.md §5, 15 divergences (14 drawn; D5 "round cap, both 8" omitted — the one place the two sides agree)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: The single largest headline is D8: embedding is entirely absent from the paper's description of MRAgent itself (it only appears describing baselines), yet is load-bearing at three separate points in the code.
The paper's f_route is explicitly framed as a pruning step (D6, Eq.12) — the code never filters accumulated tool results, they only ever grow (controller.py:206-223).

D2/D3: the write side's five formally-independent LLM functions collapse into two actual API calls per session, and the 'topic' content comes straight from raw dialogue rather than the already-segmented episode set Eq.21 specifies.

Not shown here because it isn't a paper↔code divergence: code-architecture.md's claim of 'two rerank paths taking a union' is a bug in that .md file, not a methodology gap — the code only ever runs one rerank pass (see mragent-code.json's deadrank node, state=degraded).
